title: Harbour One Product Roadmap

authority.rule: Harbour One is the product and fork. Odysseus is the legacy implementation base and compatibility boundary, not a second current product name.
authority.canonical_planning: Planning Definition v2 and its durable project/revision store
authority.canonical_knowledge: One durable owner-scoped knowledge-object store exposed through the Unified Source Index
authority.coding_execution: Capability-governed Worker Gateway with interchangeable Goose, DeepSeek Harness, Codex, OpenHands and OpenCode adapters; Goose is the first pragmatic adapter and DeepSeek Harness is a developer-preview comparison spike.
harbour_one_owns: typed Inbox decisions and work signals
policy gates, projections, receipts and evidence
worker registry, capability-policy resolution, per-job leases and result intake
harbour_one_does_not_own: a worker's long-lived agent session, memory, scheduler or model intelligence as a second product truth
direct tool authorization without the Harbour policy resolver
execution inside Harbour One, its database pod or the host control-plane pod
Git or deployment effects without an explicit adapter and gate

transition_rules: Keep odysseus.* API and schema identifiers as compatibility identifiers until a versioned migration exists; do not mass-rename them.
Markdown roadmaps remain import/export and historical evidence, but cease to be mutable project authority after migration.

Historical coding-agent and sandbox roadmaps remain compatibility and safety evidence. Reframe their worker isolation, queue, lifecycle and receipt contracts for the active Worker Gateway; do not mass-archive or reactivate them as a competing Harbour control plane.
No live provider, executor, publication or deployment action follows from this roadmap-authoring decision.

user_authorized_execution_policy.long_running_workers: A 10–15 hour run uses a fresh temporary Git worktree. It is integrated only after tests and independent review through an explicit path-scoped commit/cherry-pick; no automatic merge into another worktree occurs.
user_authorized_execution_policy.short_scoped_work: A narrow single-writer claim may use the current checkout only when its files and baseline are exclusive and its commit can be isolated from unrelated work.
user_authorized_execution_policy.internet: Default deny. An internet request must be visible in chat and state why it is needed, the intended destination/operation, the data classification, expected effect and whether it is reversible; it requires user confirmation before the worker receives access.
user_authorized_execution_policy.private_context: There is no general context-size limit for code and Planning documents. Any content tagged private requires a user chat confirmation before it is included in a context pack or sent to an external executor.

slices.name: Product identity and execution boundary
slices.objective: Make Harbour One the product/control plane, Odysseus the legacy base, and capability-governed isolated workers the temporary coding execution plane.
slices.done_when: Canonical roadmaps and execution guidance state one consistent boundary and preserve versioned compatibility aliases.

slices.name: Planning Definition v2 foundation
slices.objective: Retain the existing validated Planning Definition v2 schema, revision contracts, API, UI and MCP foundations.
slices.done_when: The foundation remains regression-tested and all new planning work targets it instead of creating another authority.

slices.name: Durable canonical Planning writer
slices.objective: Unify Planning Definition v2, project storage and revision history behind one authenticated durable writer with save, undo and conflict semantics.
slices.done_when: A fresh architecture names one store, one writer, migration rules and exact acceptance tests; the default app can persist and read back owner-scoped revisions.
slices.status_note: Fresh 2026-09-05 parent acceptance binds current raw app/route/store/authority/test bytes to 560 passing tests and independent deep review. The default app composes one browser-admin owner-scoped durable writer with save/readback/undo/conflict behavior; legacy draft writes remain unavailable. Historical r2 baseline pins and the earlier planning reconciliation are preserved. H1R-03 migration, UI, provisioning and live deployment remain separate unverified outcomes.

slices.name: Roadmap migration and Markdown demotion
slices.objective: Inventory current JSON/Markdown planning sources, migrate active project state into canonical Planning, and retain Markdown only as import, export, render and historical evidence.
slices.done_when: Every active project has a deterministic migration receipt, source classification and round-trip export; runtime inventory no longer treats editable Markdown as competing truth.
slices.status_note: The repository-only H1R-03 parent milestone promotes the predecessor acceptance recorded at docs/plans/handoffs/abc-open-work-5h-run-20260905.json#completion_campaign_20261001.h1r03_repo_parent_acceptance. Its scope is one declared active project (fuzzy/harbour-one) and six frozen primary roadmaps, including migration receipts, source classification, JSON/Markdown round-trip exports, durable heads/revisions, and normal app startup/shutdown/restart. Acceptance of any authority-successor tuple is recorded separately in runstate against its exact nine-path hashes, current tests, and independent review; the predecessor tests do not establish successor acceptance. UI, live deployment, and private-source migration are outside this recorded parent scope; H1R-04 has a separate docs-only classification; the complete Knowledge boundary remains open.

slices.name: Knowledge object and storage boundary
slices.objective: Define one owner-scoped durable knowledge-object model covering provenance, source revisions, links, retention and Planning/Forge references.
slices.done_when: A reviewed contract reconciles personal memory, RAPTOR/GraphRAG projections, USI documents and imported sources without granting projections write authority.
slices.status_note: Accepted on 2026-10-02 for the docs-only product classification and roadmap-authoring boundary. This records no complete Knowledge boundary, private-source migration, UI integration or live activation; H1R-05 remains in progress.

slices.name: Durable knowledge store and active USI
slices.objective: Replace synthetic or process-local knowledge state with the durable store and activate the Unified Source Index through explicit migration and rollback gates.
slices.done_when: A fresh reviewed architecture and path claim implement the user-authorized migration with deterministic receipts and rollback. Restart, owner-isolation, provenance, retention and stale-index tests pass against durable storage; projections cannot silently mutate canonical knowledge; existing canonical source bytes and actual private user artifacts are not automatically deleted.
slices.status_note: Accepted repository-only on 2026-10-03 from the immutable closed-map receipt: the current reviewed parent and the combined Knowledge/MCP machine receipts bind deterministic migration, rollback, restart, owner-isolation, provenance, retention, stale-index and read-only projection evidence. Private-source cutover, UI, live deployment, provider behavior, temporal verification and whole-product acceptance remain outside this result.

slices.name: Forge project/version/provider foundation
slices.objective: Retain Forge local project/version/outbox and offline provider foundations.
slices.done_when: Existing offline and provider tests remain green and all live writes remain separately gated.

slices.name: Forge memory and code context assembler
slices.objective: Assemble revision-bound project, plan, knowledge and exact-code context for humans and external coding executors.
slices.done_when: Context packs are owner-scoped, provenance-bound, reproducible and reject stale plan/code revisions; code and Planning documents have no general size limit; a private-tagged item requires a user chat confirmation before disclosure; no context pack becomes authority.

slices.name: Inbox document workbench foundation
slices.objective: Retain owner-scoped document browsing, preview, snapshots, working copies and dry-run routing foundations.
slices.done_when: The current foundation remains covered while product status text is reconciled with the implementation.
slices.status_note: The document workbench foundation is present and the canonical Open Work queue excludes accepted UIX-ABC13 through UIX-ABC24. This is not acceptance of the cross-domain typed Inbox in H1R-09 or evidence of a current live/private-source deployment.

slices.name: Unified typed Inbox
slices.objective: Unify documents, planning decisions, reviews, blockers and external source signals in one typed Inbox without merging their authorities.
slices.done_when: One read model presents source, owner, required action, due state, authority and receipt links; mutations route to the owning subsystem and are idempotent.

slices.name: Nextcloud offline source foundation
slices.objective: Retain redacted offline planning, dry-run and guarded WebDAV/transfer contracts.
slices.done_when: Offline fixtures and no-live-write defaults remain green.

slices.name: Nextcloud knowledge ingestion pilot
slices.objective: Implement deterministic extraction, dedupe and durable knowledge writes offline, then run one bounded read-only or reversible pilot after explicit approval.
slices.done_when: Fixtures prove idempotency, provenance, owner isolation and rollback; a separately authorized pilot has redacted readback evidence.

slices.name: External coding executor protocol
slices.objective: Define a capability-based Worker Gateway: job manifest, worker registry, capability registry/policy resolver, short-lived lease, typed lifecycle and result receipts while Planning remains authority.
slices.done_when: The contract fixes project/plan/worktree/capability/budget bindings, brokered tool policy, identity, revision binding, idempotency, pause/cancel races, structured receipts and fail-closed no-send defaults. Internet is default-deny and each requested access is chat-visible with reason, destination/operation, data classification, expected effect and reversibility before user confirmation. Worker loops and sandboxes remain temporary isolated executor components, never Harbour truth.

slices.name: Goose executor adapter and DeepSeek Harness comparison
slices.objective: Implement the first Goose adapter and run the same fake-worker acceptance suite against a DeepSeek Harness developer-preview spike; keep Codex, OpenHands and OpenCode as registry candidates.
slices.done_when: Fake-worker tests prove context in, policy-limited tools, reconnect-safe status, timeout/cancel, Diff/Test/Log/Review receipts and no access beyond the worktree. No external dispatch occurs without its own activation gate.

slices.name: Harbour One workspace convergence
slices.objective: Converge Planning, Knowledge, Forge, Inbox, Nextcloud and executor evidence into the Harbour One product surface.
slices.done_when: User-approved navigation and workflows use live owner-scoped read models, show freshness and authority, and contain no demo-data shadow truth.

slices.name: Legacy runtime containment
slices.objective: Reframe legacy runtime and sandbox paths into an isolated Worker Gateway lane while retaining reusable policy, receipt and compatibility contracts.
slices.done_when: Every 10–15 hour worker run uses a fresh temporary Git worktree and integrates only a reviewed, path-scoped commit/cherry-pick. Every worker runs outside Harbour/DB/host pods in a rootless disposable environment with read-only system, no privileged/container-socket/host namespace access, default-deny network, bounded resources and no long-lived secrets. Lease/token authority is explicitly documented as complementary to—not a substitute for—isolation and prompt-injection defenses.

slices.name: Golden product flow and release evidence
slices.objective: Verify a local golden flow from captured intent through Planning, knowledge/Forge context, Inbox decision and external executor evidence; keep deployment separate.
slices.done_when: Automated local evidence is green, independent review passes, user-visible acceptance is recorded and deployment remains an explicit separate decision.

next_frontier.selection_rule: Harbour One is selected only after higher-ranked Open Work items are accepted, deferred or recorded blocked. Within Harbour, preserve accepted slices and select the first still-open dependency-ready H1R item; this ordering never grants a live or external-action Go.
next_frontier.rule: Freeze and independently review exact architecture and path claims before implementation. Do not infer live authority from dependency readiness.
